title: Career Roadmap: Research Associate
summary: A Research Associate supports and conducts structured research to investigate economic, social, behavioural, and policy-related questions. With a B.Sc. in Econometrics or Economics (Honours), you can build a career analysing datasets, testing hypotheses, reviewing academic literature, evaluating policies, and preparing research reports.

blocks.text: This career is especially suitable for students who enjoy economics, statistics, analytical thinking, evidence-based decision-making, and understanding how societies and markets work.
Career snapshot

blocks.label: Entry qualification
blocks.text: B.Sc. in Econometrics, Economics, Statistics, or a related quantitative discipline

blocks.label: Core skills
blocks.text: Research methodology, econometrics, statistics, data analysis, and academic writing

blocks.label: Typical work

blocks.label: Employers
blocks.text: Universities, economic research institutes, think tanks, consulting firms, government research projects, and development organisations

blocks.label: Career objective
blocks.text: Produce reliable evidence to explain economic and social issues and inform decisions

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: Job titles vary across institutions. Some organisations use Research Associate for early-career positions, while others require a master's degree, research experience, or a Ph.D. Check the eligibility criteria for each vacancy.

Develop three or four projects that demonstrate how you turn a research question into defensible findings.
Project 1 — Inflation and economic growth
Investigate how inflation and GDP growth have moved together in India over a defined period.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: Public data collection, time-series visualisation, correlation, regression, interpretation.
Project 2 — Education and employment outcomes
Analyse how education levels relate to employment or wages using a suitable public dataset.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: Regression, confounding variables, subgroup comparisons, research limitations.
Project 3 — Public policy evaluation
Evaluate a policy question using an appropriate comparison group and a clearly defined research design.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: Research design, causal inference fundamentals, robustness checks, policy interpretation.
Project 4 — Systematic literature review
Review published studies on a topic such as youth unemployment, financial inclusion, or access to education.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: Literature search, source evaluation, synthesis, referencing, structured writing.

For every project, include the research question, dataset source, variables, methodology, results, limitations, and reproducible code where applicable. Clearly distinguish association from causation; a regression result alone does not prove that one variable caused another.

blocks.text: Useful starting points include the MIT OpenCourseWare economics courses and World Bank Open Learning Campus. Prioritise courses with exercises or projects that you can demonstrate in your portfolio.
Search for these roles:

Look at university economics departments, public-policy institutions, think tanks, economic consulting firms, development organisations, and research projects funded by public or private institutions.

For Indian opportunities, also review research-project vacancies at universities and economic research institutes. Eligibility can differ significantly: some roles accept a bachelor's degree, while others require a master's degree or prior research experience.

blocks.label: Interview preparation
blocks.text: Be ready to explain a regression output, interpret a confidence interval, clean a dataset, discuss a paper you have read, and justify the methodology used in your own project.

items.text: Entry level — Research Assistant / Junior Research Associate

blocks.text: Collect data, review literature, run basic statistical analyses, and assist with research reports.

items.text: Experienced researcher — Research Associate / Research Analyst

blocks.text: Manage analytical tasks, conduct empirical analysis, and contribute to papers, reports, and presentations.

items.text: Specialist — Economist, Policy Analyst, or Senior Researcher

blocks.text: Develop expertise in areas such as labour economics, development, public finance, or economic forecasting. Requirements vary by role.

items.text: Long-term — Research Fellow, Principal Researcher, or Academic

blocks.text: Lead research programmes or pursue academic research. Independent and senior research positions often require postgraduate study and substantial experience; academic careers commonly require a Ph.D.
Research salaries vary according to the institution, funding source, location, degree requirements, and whether the appointment is temporary or permanent.

When comparing vacancies, check the stated monthly remuneration, contract duration, benefits, required qualifications, and opportunities for publication or further study. Government-funded research projects may specify remuneration directly in the recruitment notice.

blocks.label: Final recommendation
blocks.text: Build a foundation in economics, statistics, and econometrics, then complete one rigorous empirical research project using public data. Pair that project with clear academic writing and an internship or faculty-supervised research experience. This will help you demonstrate research readiness for entry-level opportunities while identifying whether postgraduate study is necessary for your preferred specialisation.
